title: Tian – Made Ahead With Beautiful Presentation
description: Make-Ahead Vegetable Tian is as delicious to eat as it is beautiful to present. Imagine layered alternating potatoes, zucchini and tomatoes sitting atop luscious, caramelized onions topped with Gruyère cheese. (The topping could instead be a mixture of breadcrumbs and parmesan.) The vegetable tian is the perfect side dish to serve for a special occasion or anytime for that matter. What's even better is that the leftovers, if any are just as amazing. (You could also add some eggplant slices, salted then damped dry.)
ingredients: 1 ¼ pounds onions, sliced (2 large onions)
1 ¼ pounds Yukon Gold potatoes, optionally peeled and sliced ¼-inch thick
1 large zucchini (12 – 14 ounces), sliced ¼-inch thick
6 Roma tomatoes (1 ¼-pounds), sliced ¼-inch thick, or big tomatoes with the slices cut in half
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, divided
2 teaspoons olive oil for drizzling on tian
directions: Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over low to medium heat. Add onions, ¾ teaspoon of salt, ¼ teaspoon of dried thyme, and ¼ teaspoon of black pepper. Cook over for about 20 minutes, stirring regularly, until caramelized and colored. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds or until the garlic is fragrant. Transfer to 2 ½-quart casserole dish that has been sprayed with non-stick spray.

Meanwhile, bring a large saucepan of water with 1 tablespoon of salt to a boil. Add potatoes; cook for about 5 minutes. Remove the potatoes or drain, saving the water. Place a single layer on a paper towel-lined baking sheet. Blot dry with paper towels.
Use the hot water to blanch the zucchini or a minute of two, then drain and blot dry.
Salt the tomatoes, blotting dry before assembly.

Layer upright potato, zucchini, and tomato alternately on top of the onions fitting the layers upright. Cover the onions completely. Drizzle with 2 teaspoons of olive oil. Sprinkle with ¼ teaspoon each of dried thyme, dried basil, and dried oregano. Cover with aluminum foil.

May be prepared in advance up to this point and refrigerated. Or, cook the first 35 minutes, as below, then cool and refrigerate, maybe overnight. If you go this route, bring it out of the frig and get to room temperature for about an hour before the final uncovered baking with the cheese.

Otherwise, preheat oven to 400°F. Bake vegetable Tian covered for 35 minutes. Remove from oven; remove aluminum foil. Sprinkle with cheese. Return uncovered to 425°F oven for an additional 5 to 10 minutes, and everything is browned and beautiful.
